header.userPrompt:
Upgrade the chimp dependency from `com.softwaremill.chimp %% core % 0.1.8` to the
current release. The library was reorganised into several modules and its API
changed, so this is a refactoring, not a version bump.

Facts verified against Maven Central and the chimp 0.5.2 README — treat them as
a starting point, and check the real API in the docs
(https://chimp.softwaremill.com/) and in the artifact sources before writing code:

- Latest version is 0.5.2. The old `core` artifact no longer exists. The modules
  are now `chimp-core`, `chimp-server`, `chimp-client`, plus
  `chimp-{server,client}-{ox,zio,pekko}` integration modules. Orca only hosts MCP
  servers, so `"com.softwaremill.chimp" %% "chimp-server" % "0.5.2"` is the
  baseline; reach for `chimp-server-ox` only if something orca needs actually
  requires the streaming/bidirectional API.
- Packages moved: `import chimp.*` becomes `import chimp.server.*`, with protocol
  types under `chimp.protocol.*`.
- Endpoint construction changed: `mcpEndpoint(tools, List("mcp"))` becomes
  `McpServer(tools = tools).endpoint(List("mcp"))`.
- Tool handlers no longer return `Either[String, String]`; they return
  `ToolResult` (e.g. `ToolResult.text(...)`).

Affected code: everything under `tools/src/main/scala/orca/backend/mcp/`
(`McpHost`, `AskUserMcpServer`, `GitHubMcpServer`, `RepoMcpServer`),
`tools/src/test/scala/orca/backend/mcp/McpHostTest.scala`,
`project/Dependencies.scala` and `build.sbt`.

Requirements:

- Behaviour must not change. In particular `McpHost` must keep both of its
  guarantees on every tool it binds: output truncated at
  `McpHost.MaxOutputChars` on the success and the error channel alike, and a
  handler that throws turned into a tool error rather than a transport failure
  the agent cannot read. Express those over the new result type; do not drop the
  error channel. Netty request and idle timeouts stay as they are.
- Update the dependency declaration and the explanatory comments in
  `project/Dependencies.scala` and `build.sbt` so they describe the modules
  actually used.
- Update `adr/0012-mcp-host-bridge.md`. It names chimp 0.1.8 and states that the
  module ships HTTP only with no stdio transport — both are now wrong, since
  0.5.2 ships a stdio transport. Keep the ADR's decision as it stands; correct
  the facts and the version, and keep the edit minimal.
- The whole project must compile and the full test suite must pass.

resultJson.description:
Orca hosts three small MCP servers in-process (`ask_user`, the GitHub issue reader, and the two git read tools) so agent turns with no shell can still reach host-side capabilities. All three are built on chimp, pinned at `com.softwaremill.chimp %% core % 0.1.8`. That artifact no longer exists: chimp was split into `chimp-core` / `chimp-server` / `chimp-client` plus per-effect-system integration modules, and the current release is 0.5.2. This is a refactoring, not a version bump — the package moved to `chimp.server.*`, `mcpEndpoint(tools, path)` became `McpServer(tools = tools).endpoint(path)`, and tool handlers now return a `ToolResult` carrying content blocks and an `isError` flag instead of `Either[String, String]`.

The goal is to land that migration with no observable change in behaviour. `McpHost` is the piece that matters: it wraps every tool it binds in a guard giving two structural guarantees — output cut at `McpHost.MaxOutputChars` on the success channel *and* the error channel, and a handler that throws turned into a readable tool error rather than a transport failure the agent cannot parse. Both must survive the move onto the new result type; the error channel must not be dropped. Netty's request and idle timeouts stay as they are, and `McpHost.start` / the three `start` methods keep their signatures, so the claude, codex, gemini and pi backends need no edits.

Two corrections travel with it: chimp-server 0.5.2 compiles against tapir 1.13.31 while orca pins 1.13.25, so the build needs realigning; and ADR 0012 records facts the upgrade falsifies (it names chimp 0.1.8 and claims the module ships HTTP only — 0.5.2 ships a stdio transport). The ADR's decision stands on its other, independent reason; only the facts change.

tasks.title: Bump tapir to 1.13.31 to match chimp 0.5.2
tasks.description:
In `project/Dependencies.scala`, change `val tapir = "1.13.25"` to `"1.13.31"`.

chimp-server 0.5.2 declares tapir-core, tapir-json-circe and tapir-apispec-docs at 1.13.31 as compile dependencies, while orca pins tapir-apispec-docs and tapir-netty-server-sync at 1.13.25. Under sbt's latest-wins conflict manager, swapping in chimp without this bump leaves tapir-core at 1.13.31 and tapir-netty-server-sync at 1.13.25 — a mixed-version tapir classpath. 1.13.31 is also the current tapir release. Doing it first keeps any tapir-side breakage separable from the chimp migration.

`V.sttpApispec` is already 0.11.10, which is what chimp-server 0.5.2 uses — leave it. No source changes expected; fix any that the bump forces.

Done when: `sbt compile` and `sbt test` pass on the whole project.

tasks.title: Swap chimp core 0.1.8 for chimp-server 0.5.2 and migrate orca.backend.mcp
tasks.description:
One atomic change — the `tools` module will not compile part-way through, so the build swap and all five source files move together.

**Build.** `V.chimp` to `"0.5.2"`; `val chimp = "com.softwaremill.chimp" %% "chimp-server" % V.chimp`. Rewrite its comment to describe what is used: chimp-server supplies the MCP server endpoint as a Tapir `ServerEndpoint`, paired with the Netty-sync interpreter. Do **not** add `chimp-server-ox` — that module only adds the streaming/bidirectional transports; orca uses plain request/response HTTP, which the base module ships. Fix the `tools` module comment in `build.sbt` (~line 86) only where the module rename makes it wrong; its point about the server being shared across backends still holds.

**`McpHost.scala`.** Imports become `chimp.server.{McpServer, ServerContext, ServerTool, ToolResult}` plus `chimp.protocol.ToolContent`.
- `guarded` now takes `ServerTool[I, O, Identity, ServerContext[Identity]]`; its `logic` field is `(I, ServerContext[Identity], Seq[Header]) => ToolResult[O]` — three arguments now, `Header` is `sttp.model.Header`. `ServerTool` is still a case class, so the existing `t.copy(logic = ...)` shape carries over.
- Both guarantees, expressed over `ToolResult`: truncate the `text` of every `ToolContent.Text` in `result.content` **regardless of `isError`** — that is the new form of "both channels" — and catch `NonFatal` into a truncated `ToolResult.error(...)`, keeping the current message derivation (`Option(e.getMessage).getOrElse(e.toString)`). `ToolResult` is covariant in `O`, so `ToolResult.error(...): ToolResult[Nothing]` fits wherever `ToolResult[O]` is wanted. `structuredContent` needs no handling — no orca tool declares an output schema.
- `start`'s endpoint line becomes `McpServer(tools = tools.map(t => guarded(t))).endpoint(List("mcp"))`. Keep the explicit `t => guarded(t)` lambda rather than eta-expanding to `map(guarded)`: the list element type now has two wildcards, and the lambda is what lets them be captured. `McpServer`'s `name` / `version` / `showJsonSchemaMetadata` defaults are identical to 0.1.8's `mcpEndpoint` defaults — leave them, the advertised server identity does not change.
- Unchanged: `.port(0)`, `requestTimeout(toolTimeout)`, `idleTimeout(toolTimeout + 1.minute)`, the `useCloseableInScope` registration, the idempotent-`close()` `AtomicBoolean`, and the public shape of `start`.
- Update the scaladoc on `MaxOutputChars`, `bounded`, `guardedResult` and `guarded` wherever the new type falsifies the wording; keep it as terse as it is.

**The three servers.** `import chimp.*` becomes `import chimp.server.*`. `ask_user` returns `ToolResult.text(bridge.ask(in.question))`. The GitHub and git tools keep their `Either`-shaped inner logic — `IssueHandle.parse`, `git.show`, `git.fileAt` all return `Either` — and convert at the boundary with `ToolResult.fromEither`, which is exactly `fold(error, text)`, the mapping chimp 0.1.8 applied internally. Remove `RepoMcpServer.scala:82`'s `private type ToolResult = Either[String, String]`: a one-use alias that now collides with `chimp.server.ToolResult`. Leave `GitShowInput.paths`/`stat` as `Option` (`RepoMcpServerTest` pins that), and leave every `ServerName` / `ToolSlug` / `ToolTimeout` / `Hint` value untouched.

**`McpHostTest.scala`.** `resultOf` returns a `ToolResult`; the direct `logic` call needs the new middle argument, `ServerContext.noop[Identity]`. Rewrite the four guard assertions to read `isError` and the text of `content` instead of `Either`. The fifth — the over-the-wire test proving `start` installs the guard — keeps its assertions verbatim (status 200, body contains the message, body contains `cut after <MaxOutputChars> char`). All five scenarios must stay covered: at-cap passthrough, one-over-cap cut with the marker, oversized **error** cut, throw-becomes-tool-error, wire-level check.

Done when: `sbt compile` and the full `sbt test` pass — including the two live-HTTP tests, `AskUserMcpServerTest`'s `tools/list` and `McpHostTest`'s `tools/call` — `sbt scalafmtCheckAll` is clean, and there are zero compiler warnings.

tasks.title: Correct ADR 0012's stale chimp facts
tasks.description:
`adr/0012-mcp-host-bridge.md` records four things the upgrade falsifies. Correct them in place; the decision itself does not change.

1. **"Why chimp" (~line 93):** "Pinned to `0.1.8` — bumped Tapir to `1.13.18` and Ox to `1.0.2` to keep the classpath single-resolved." Update to what the build actually holds after this epic (chimp 0.5.2, tapir 1.13.31), keeping the sentence's point that the chimp pin drives the tapir pin.
2. **"Why HTTP transport, not stdio", reason 2 (~line 105):** "The chimp 0.1.8 module ships HTTP only; the stdio transport would need separate machinery." Wrong now — `chimp-server` 0.5.2 ships `ServerStdioTransport` alongside `ServerHttpTransport` (only the streaming variants live in the per-effect-system modules). Correct the fact rather than deleting the section: reason 1 is independent and still load-bearing (a stdio server is spawned by the agent CLI itself, so the `ask_user` handler would need a side-channel back to the orca process; HTTP on 127.0.0.1 is one fewer indirection).
3. **Components, `AskUserMcpServer` bullet (~line 49):** it says the server "wraps chimp's `mcpEndpoint`" — now `McpServer(...).endpoint(...)`.
4. **Same bullet (~line 52):** "The handler is `in => Right(bridge.ask(in.question))`" — now `ToolResult.text(...)`.

3 and 4 are a couple of words each; fix them so the ADR does not name an API that no longer exists. Out of scope: the same bullets place the code in `orca.tools.claude.mcp` when it actually lives in `orca.backend.mcp` — pre-existing drift, unrelated to chimp, leave it.

The file already carries an inline `> **Correction (measured against ...)**` block from an earlier revision; match whatever reads naturally, but do not restructure the ADR or touch Consequences / Future work.

Docs only — no code, no build changes.

resultJson.brief:
## Modules and directories

- `tools/` (`orca-tools`) — the only module that touches chimp. Hosts the cross-backend `orca.backend` package, which is why the MCP servers live here rather than in a backend module.
- `tools/src/main/scala/orca/backend/mcp/` — the MCP host and the three servers.
- `claude/`, `codex/`, `gemini/`, `pi/`, `runner/` — consumers. They reach the servers only through orca's own `start` signatures and **import nothing from chimp**. Keep those signatures and no downstream edit is needed.

## Files

Change:
- `tools/src/main/scala/orca/backend/mcp/McpHost.scala` — the Netty binding plus the `guarded` wrapper carrying both guarantees.
- `.../mcp/AskUserMcpServer.scala`, `GitHubMcpServer.scala`, `RepoMcpServer.scala` — the tool definitions.
- `tools/src/test/scala/orca/backend/mcp/McpHostTest.scala` — calls `ServerTool.logic` directly, so it moves with the API.
- `project/Dependencies.scala` (`V.chimp`, `V.tapir`, the `val chimp` coordinate and its comment); `build.sbt` ~line 86 (the `tools` module comment about chimp).
- `adr/0012-mcp-host-bridge.md`.

Read, do not change:
- `.../mcp/{AskUserMcpServerTest,RepoMcpServerTest,GitHubMcpServerTest}.scala` — must keep passing untouched. `AskUserMcpServerTest` does a live `tools/list` POST; `RepoMcpServerTest` pins `GitShowInput.paths`/`stat` as `Option` (a derived circe codec rejects a missing non-`Option` field even when Scala declares a default).
- `.../mcp/{AskUserBridge,AskUserSession}.scala` — no chimp types.
- `AGENTS.md` names `GitHubMcpServer` once, in a tool-tiering list. It asserts nothing about chimp or the handler result type — verified, needs no edit.

## chimp 0.5.2 API

`"com.softwaremill.chimp" %% "chimp-server" % "0.5.2"`. Compile deps: chimp-core (circe 0.14.16 — the source of the `io.circe.Codec` derivation orca already relies on — plus slf4j-api 2.0.18), tapir-core / tapir-json-circe / tapir-apispec-docs **1.13.31**, sttp.apispec jsonschema-circe 0.11.10 (already orca's pin). `tapir-netty-server-sync` stays orca-declared.

`chimp-server-ox` supplies only the streaming/bidirectional transports (`OxServerHttpTransport`, `OxServerStdioTransport`). Orca needs neither.

Packages: `chimp.server.*` — `tool`, `ServerTool`, `ToolResult`, `McpServer`, `ServerContext`, `OriginCheck`, transports. `chimp.protocol.*` — `ToolContent` and the JSON-RPC types. (The published *quickstart* page shows `import chimp.*`; that is a doc slip — the source tree is `server/src/main/scala/chimp/server/` and the *tools* page shows `import chimp.server.*`.)

```scala
// chimp.server
def tool(name: String): PartialTool          // name: ^[A-Za-z0-9_./-]+$, 1-64 chars
// PartialTool: .description(String), .withAnnotations(ToolAnnotations),
//              .input[I: Schema: Decoder]: Tool[I, NoStructuredOutput]
// Tool[I, O]:
def handle(logic: I => ToolResult[O]): ServerTool[I, O, Identity, ServerContext[Identity]]
def handleWithHeaders(logic: (I, Seq[Header]) => ToolResult[O]): ServerTool[I, O, Identity, ServerContext[Identity]]

case class ServerTool[I, O, F[_], -C <: ServerContext[F]](
    name: String, description: Option[String], inputSchema: ToolSchema,
    inputDecoder: Decoder[I], outputSchema: Option[ToolSchema],
    annotations: Option[ToolAnnotations],
    logic: (I, C, Seq[Header]) => F[ToolResult[O]])   // was (I, Seq[Header]) => F[Either[String, String]]

case class ToolResult[+O](content: List[ToolContent],
                          structuredContent: Option[Json] = None,
                          isError: Boolean = false):
  def asError: ToolResult[O]
  def withStructured[O2: Encoder](value: O2): ToolResult[O2]
object ToolResult:
  def text(text: String): ToolResult[NoStructuredOutput]
  def error(message: String): ToolResult[Nothing]
  def fromEither(r: Either[String, String]): ToolResult[NoStructuredOutput] // = r.fold(error, text)
  def content(content: ToolContent*): ToolResult[NoStructuredOutput]
  // also image, audio, embedded, structured

case class McpServer[F[_]](
    name: String = "Chimp MCP server", version: String = "1.0.0",
    instructions: Option[String] = None, showJsonSchemaMetadata: Boolean = true,
    originCheck: OriginCheck = OriginCheck.localhostOnly,
    tools: List[ServerTool[?, ?, F, ServerContext[F]]] = Nil, /* prompts, resources, ... */):
  def endpoint(path: List[String]): ServerEndpoint[Any, F]   // = ServerHttpTransport(path).serve(this)

trait ServerContext[F[_]]
object ServerContext:
  def noop[F[_]]: ServerContext[F]

// chimp.protocol
enum ToolContent:
  case Text(`type`: String = "text", text: String)
  case Image(...); case Audio(...); case ResourceContent(...); case ResourceLink(...)
```

`Header` is `sttp.model.Header`; `Identity` stays `sttp.shared.Identity`. Builder order is unchanged: `tool(slug).description(...).input[I].handle(...)`.

## Behaviour-parity facts (verified)

- 0.1.8's `mcpEndpoint[F](tools, path, name = "Chimp MCP server", version = "1.0.0", showJsonSchemaMetadata = true)` has **identical** defaults to `McpServer`'s. Passing nothing extra preserves the advertised server identity exactly.
- `ToolResult.fromEither` is literally `fold(error, text)` — the same success/error mapping the old `Either[String, String]` logic received. It is the natural boundary conversion for `GitHubMcpServer.read` and `RepoMcpServer.render`.
- Truncating \"both channels\" now means bounding the `text` of every `ToolContent.Text` in `content`, independent of `isError`. `structuredContent` is always `None` — no orca tool calls `.output[...]`.
- `OriginCheck.localhostOnly` is a new default and admits orca's traffic: a missing `Origin` passes (`origin.forall(allowed)` over an empty `Option`), and `Host` must be localhost / 127.0.0.1 / [::1] / ::1, which the `http://127.0.0.1:$port/mcp` binding satisfies. Leave it at the default.
- The HTTP transport is a `POST` at the configured path returning `Option[Json]` with an explicit status code, with no `initialize`-handshake or session-id gate visible — consistent with the existing tests POSTing `tools/call` and `tools/list` cold. Running them confirms it.

## Gotchas

- `RepoMcpServer.scala:82` has `private type ToolResult = Either[String, String]`, which collides with `chimp.server.ToolResult` under the new import. One use — delete it.
- `McpHost.start` maps over `List[ServerTool[?, ?, Identity, ServerContext[Identity]]]`: keep the explicit `t => guarded(t)` lambda (already there for the same reason with one wildcard); eta-expanding to `map(guarded)` can fail to capture two wildcards.
- `McpHostTest` calls `ServerTool.logic` directly to test the guard off the wire — the new middle argument is `ServerContext.noop[Identity]`. Read results via `result.isError` and `result.content.collect { case ToolContent.Text(_, t) => t }`.
- Netty config stays byte-for-byte: `.port(0).modifyConfig(_.requestTimeout(toolTimeout).idleTimeout(toolTimeout + 1.minute))`. The extra minute exists because Netty requires the idle timeout to exceed the request timeout.
- `McpHost.guarded` is `private[mcp]` purely so the test can reach it — keep that visibility. The `useCloseableInScope` registration and idempotent-`close()` `AtomicBoolean` are unrelated to chimp; leave them.
- The `com.softwaremill.chimp` logger entries in `runner/src/main/resources/logback.xml` and `claude/src/test/resources/logback-test.xml` are dead and always were — chimp's logger is `chimp.server.McpHandler` (was `chimp.McpHandler`), it logs only at DEBUG, and both configs root at WARN. Pre-existing and harmless: **out of scope.**
- A repo-wide grep for \"chimp\" also hits `.orca/progress-*.json` — a run log, not code.

## Conventions

- Scala 3, braceless syntax. Explicit return types on public `def`/`val`. Deliberate visibility on every top-level declaration — follow the `private[orca]` / `private[mcp]` markers already in these files.
- Comments state only what is not obvious from the code and never restate it. The existing scaladoc is the model; preserve its intent and update anything the new API falsifies.
- munit tests, one scenario each, no redundancy.
- Verify with `sbt compile`, `sbt test`, or `sbt \"tools/testOnly orca.backend.mcp.*\"` to scope. `sbt scalafmtAll` to format, `sbt scalafmtCheckAll` is the gate. Zero compiler warnings is enforced (`-Wunused:all`, `-Wvalue-discard`, `-Wnonunit-statement`) — a leftover unused import fails the build.
- Integration tests are gated behind `ORCA_INTEGRATION=1` and skip by default; plain `sbt test` is the bar."

- `RepoMcpServer.scala:82` has `private type ToolResult = Either[String, String]`, which collides with `chimp.server.ToolResult` under the new import. One use — delete it.
- `McpHost.start` maps over `List[ServerTool[?, ?, Identity, ServerContext[Identity]]]`: keep the explicit `t => guarded(t)` lambda (already there for the same reason with one wildcard); eta-expanding to `map(guarded)` can fail to capture two wildcards.
- `McpHostTest` calls `ServerTool.logic` directly to test the guard off the wire — the new middle argument is `ServerContext.noop[Identity]`. Read results via `result.isError` and `result.content.collect { case ToolContent.Text(_, t) => t }`.
- Netty config stays byte-for-byte: `.port(0).modifyConfig(_.requestTimeout(toolTimeout).idleTimeout(toolTimeout + 1.minute))`. The extra minute exists because Netty requires the idle timeout to exceed the request timeout.
- `McpHost.guarded` is `private[mcp]` purely so the test can reach it — keep that visibility. The `useCloseableInScope` registration and idempotent-`close()` `AtomicBoolean` are unrelated to chimp; leave them.
- The `com.softwaremill.chimp` logger entries in `runner/src/main/resources/logback.xml` and `claude/src/test/resources/logback-test.xml` are dead and always were — chimp's logger is `chimp.server.McpHandler` (was `chimp.McpHandler`), it logs only at DEBUG, and both configs root at WARN. Pre-existing and harmless: **out of scope.**
- A repo-wide grep for \"chimp\" also hits `.orca/progress-*.json` — a run log, not code.

## Conventions

- Scala 3, braceless syntax. Explicit return types on public `def`/`val`. Deliberate visibility on every top-level declaration — follow the `private[orca]` / `private[mcp]` markers already in these files.
- Comments state only what is not obvious from the code and never restate it. The existing scaladoc is the model; preserve its intent and update anything the new API falsifies.
- munit tests, one scenario each, no redundancy.
- Verify with `sbt compile`, `sbt test`, or `sbt \"tools/testOnly orca.backend.mcp.*\"` to scope. `sbt scalafmtAll` to format, `sbt scalafmtCheckAll` is the gate. Zero compiler warnings is enforced (`-Wunused:all`, `-Wvalue-discard`, `-Wnonunit-statement`) — a leftover unused import fails the build.
- Integration tests are gated behind `ORCA_INTEGRATION=1` and skip by default; plain `sbt test` is the bar."
